title: Columnar formats and read optimisation: Parquet and ORC

videos.script: Lesson five wrote the clicks as Parquet, and the copy came out larger than the gzipped CSV it came from. {{surprise}} This lesson opens the files to find out why. A Parquet file stores each column apart, in row groups, with a footer that says what every column chunk holds. {{footer}} Change three things about how January is written: the codec, the type of the timestamps, and the page format. The month falls from thirty-three megabytes to seven. {{seven}} Then sort the data by book, and a filter on the rarest books reads one million rows instead of twenty-four, while the files grow by a quarter. {{sort}} Every choice here is made when the data is written, and paid for every time it is read. {{choice}}
